title: Affine restriction extends the irrelevant ideal to the irrelevant ideal.
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme and let $\mathcal A$ be a quasi-coherent commutative graded $\mathcal O_X$-algebra as in [def-nagata-relative-proj]. For affine opens $W\subseteq V$, let $\rho_{V,W}:\mathcal A(V)\to\mathcal A(W)$ be the induced graded restriction homomorphism of the homogeneous section rings. Then the irrelevant homogeneous ideal $\mathcal A(W)_+=\bigoplus_{n>0}\mathcal A(W)_n$ is contained in the ideal of $\mathcal A(W)$ generated by $\rho_{V,W}(\mathcal A(V)_+)$:

$$\operatorname{HomogeneousIdeal.irrelevant}(\mathcal A(W))\subseteq\operatorname{HomogeneousIdeal.irrelevant}(\mathcal A(V)).map(\rho_{V,W}).$$

proof.text: By HomogeneousIdeal.irrelevant_le it suffices to put every section of positive homogeneous degree n on W into the mapped irrelevant ideal. Equip the total module with quasi-coherence from the input and apply affine section base change to obtain a bijective tensor map c with c(a tensor r) = r times restriction(a).

Project c(t) to degree n by the sheaf coproduct projection and reinclusion. Naturality of this module endomorphism commutes with restriction and its linearity commutes with base scalars. For a pure tensor its projected image is the product of a structural scalar and the restriction of a degree-n section on V. The latter belongs to the mapped irrelevant ideal since n is positive. Tensor induction, using ideal closure under addition and zero, proves the same membership for every tensor.

Choose a tensor mapping to the given degree-n section by surjectivity of c. Its homogeneous projection equals itself by the coproduct projection-inclusion identity. The tensor-induction result gives its required membership and hence the irrelevant-ideal inclusion.
